recognize_zh: 周邊血中兩顆淋巴球：左邊小而緻密，右邊稍大、核輪廓略不規則且胞質少；在此倍率下看不清典型腦回狀核，只能提示 Sézary 細胞，需高倍或流式細胞儀確認。
features: Two lymphoid cells: one small with dense chromatin, one slightly larger with mildly irregular nucleus
High N:C ratio with scant pale-blue agranular cytoplasm
Nuclear grooves/cerebriform folds not clearly resolved at this magnification
Normal segmented neutrophil for size comparison
Red cells with prominent central pallor; platelets present
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two lymphoid cells, one small with dense chromatin and one slightly larger with a mildly irregular nuclear outline and scant agranular cytoplasm, adjacent to a normal segmented neutrophil. The characteristic cerebriform nuclear folding is not clearly resolved at this magnification. Red cells show prominent central pallor. The lymphoid cells are compatible with, but not diagnostic of, Sézary cells; flow cytometry for CD4+ T cells with loss of CD7 and/or CD26 is required.

ddx.vs: Normal lymphocytes have smooth round nuclear contours and are not phenotypically aberrant by flow cytometry.
CLL cells have coarse clumped chromatin, frequent smudge cells and a CD5+/CD23+ B-cell phenotype.
T-PLL cells have more basophilic cytoplasm with blebs and visible nucleoli, and show TCL1 rearrangement.
